topic: Git, GitHub, Branching, and Collaborative Development
learningObjectives: Explain how Git tracks and manages source code changes.
Use branches and commits to organize development work.
Understand a collaborative GitHub workflow using pull requests.

activities.title: Git Workflow Map
activities.instruction: Click each stage to explore how a change moves through Git.

content.concept: Git tracks changes through the working directory, staging area, local repository, and remote repository.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Contains the files currently being edited.

A shared repository such as a GitHub repository.

activities.title: Command Explorer
activities.instruction: Click each Git command to learn what it does.

content.concept: Git commands perform different repository operations: git add stages changes, git commit records changes, git pull retrieves remote changes, git push uploads commits, and git clone copies a remote repository.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Stages selected changes for the next commit.
Creates a new commit containing staged changes.
Fetches changes from a remote repository and integrates them into the current branch.
Uploads local commits to a remote repository.
Creates a local copy of a remote repository.

activities.title: Branching Strategy Builder
activities.instruction: Build a simple branch structure for developing and integrating a feature.

content.concept: Branches isolate development work so features can be developed independently before being reviewed and integrated into a shared branch.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Pull Request Sequence
activities.instruction: Arrange the steps from feature development to integration.

content.concept: A pull request provides a structured workflow for reviewing and integrating changes from a development branch into a shared branch.
